pr_title: drivers: hwinfo: Fix mcux device id
pr_body:
This fixes an issue where the unique device identifier is incorrectly
copied from an address on the AHB bus to memory using memcpy.

I verified corrected behavior by comparing `hwinfo devid` command
output to memory view of the SoC using the debugger.

Fixes #48447

Signed-off-by: Bryce Wilkins <bryce.wilkins@gmail.com>
pr_comments:
> Looks good now. Thanks for the fix!

@alexanderwachter I had to push again to fix a style issue I didn't check for earlier. I'm not sure why but after pushing it says I dismissed your (stale) review. I think this needs your ✅ again. Sorry about that!

issue_context.title: `hwinfo devid` does not work correctly for NXP devices using `nxp,lpc-uid` device binding
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
`hwinfo devid` does not correctly retrieve the device UUID for NXP SoC's using the `nxp,lpc-uid` device binding and corresponding driver `drivers/hwinfo/hwinfo_mcux_syscon.c`.

The bug was introduced in #36457

Primary problem is `memcpy` is used to read bytes from an address on the AHB bus (not in RAM). In such case `memcpy` does not perform correctly -- only bytes on word-aligned (32-bit) memory addresses are read.

Secondary problem is not converting from SoC endianness (little endian) to big endian (as expected by `hwinfo devid` command).

**To Reproduce**
For the following use a board with NXP SoC for which `hwinfo devid` uses the `nxp,lpc-uid` binding and driver (`hwinfo_mcux_syscon.c`). In my case I used a custom i.MX RT685 board but Zephyr supported board `mimxrt685_evk` can also be used.
 
1. Build and flash a project for which `HWINFO` driver and shell is enabled
2. Read the device id with `hwinfo devid`
```
$ hwinfo devid
Length: 16
ID: 0x44000000f20000009c00000061000000
```
3. Compare result when using debugger to view SoC device memory
In this example, showing UUID[0-3] of i.MX RT685 starting from `0x40002F50`:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13003844/181700147-3a28320e-7d69-4027-b530-029e0b522d33.png)
 
Memory view as 32-bit (big endian) representation
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13003844/181699476-07942121-ba82-419e-855a-67e8803ded11.png)

It is clear `hwinfo devid` did not read the UUID correctly, but some similarities can be seen.

**Expected behavior**
The ID printed by `hwinfo devid` should match what is in the device.

**Environment**
 - OS: MacOS
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK
 - Zephyr version 3.1.0

review_comments:
I originally thought `nxp,lpc-uid` binding could support larger than 128b UUID, in which case it would exceed the size of `struct uid` and I wanted to ensure no writing outside the space reserved for `id`.

On second look it seems `nxp,lpc-uid` is specifically a 128b UUID. I'll remove this secondary length check and add a comment for `id` member of `struct uid`.
I would rather define the array size from the device tree reg size property.
Updated with a macro using `DT_INST_REG_SIZE(0)` for the number of UUID words.
